Bill.BriefDescription: Creating the child predatory drug act.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to creating the child predatory drug act;reenacting and amending RCW 9.94A.533; adding a new section to chapter9.94A RCW; creating new sections; and prescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: This act may be known and cited as the childpredatory drug act of 2010.

The legislature finds an alarming trendexists of the manufacture, sale, delivery, and possession of childpredatory drugs, particularly of methamphetamines, heroin, andmarijuana, that are flavored, colored, shaped, packaged, or otherwisealtered in a way that is designed with the intent to make them moreappealing to minors. Child predatory drugs are most often cheap andhighly addictive and create grave risks. The manufacture, sale,delivery, and possession of child predatory drugs are direct attemptsby predatory drug dealers to reach out and attract a younger age groupto lure them into the drug culture. Child predatory drugs are cleverlydisguised and distributed among unsuspecting minors in order to moreeasily entice them to use them. As such, child predatory drugs are p. 1 HB 2340extremely dangerous and exceptionally harmful since they can beingested by younger children who have no idea what they are consumingor why they may be experiencing serious negative effects. Flavors may include strawberry, chocolate, cola, and others that reduce the bittertaste of the drug, but do not affect the potency of the drug. Drugspackaged or disguised as candy or other more enticing objects should beconsidered serious threats by parents. Children should be advised tonot accept any candy which may resemble one of these new childpredatory drugs, to avoid any participation in distributing or usingany drugs, no matter how harmless they may seem, and to report anysuspicious activity to the appropriate authorities or a trusted adult.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9.94A RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) In a prosecution for manufacturing, selling, delivering, orpossessing with intent to manufacture, sell, or deliver a controlledsubstance listed in RCW 69.50.401, the prosecuting attorney shall filea special allegation of promoting a child predatory drug wheneversufficient admissible evidence exists, which, when considered with themost plausible, reasonably foreseeable defense that could be raisedunder the evidence, would justify a finding by a reasonable andobjective fact finder that the controlled substance was flavored,colored, shaped, packaged, or otherwise altered in a way that wasdesigned with the intent to make the controlled substance moreappealing to a minor. (2) Once a special allegation has been made under this section, thestate has the burden to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that thecontrolled substance was flavored, colored, shaped, packaged, orotherwise altered in a way that was designed with the intent to makethe controlled substance more appealing to a minor. If a jury is had,the jury shall, if it finds the defendant guilty, also find a specialverdict as to whether the controlled substance was flavored, colored,shaped, packaged, or otherwise altered in a way that was designed withthe intent to make the controlled substance more appealing to a minor.If no jury is had, the court shall make a finding of fact as to whetherthe controlled substance was flavored, colored, shaped, packaged, orotherwise altered in a way that was designed with the intent to makethe controlled substance more appealing to a minor. HB 2340 p. 2 (3) The prosecuting attorney shall not withdraw a specialallegation filed under this section without the approval of the courtthrough an order of dismissal of the allegation. The court may notdismiss the special allegation unless it finds that the order isnecessary to correct an error in the initial charging decision or thatthere are evidentiary problems that make proving the special allegationdoubtful.
